summary: Both editions were independently compared with every clause of the selected Greek working source. Both preserve the seven stone categories, agents and actions, rejection versus separation, comparative strength, middle versus outer placement, support of the interior stones, and the emphatic statement that nothing had been chipped away. The simplified edition preserves these meanings without introducing a concrete fidelity defect. The notes distinguish bracketed editorial additions from preserved wording, retain the unresolved dagger-marked crux, and disclose alternatives without replacing the selected working readings or claiming unanimous witness support. The supplied bounded reports support the corresponding disclosures; acceptance does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscript handwriting, certify exhaustive collation, or settle the unresolved Greek wording.
